892: Isma'il moves the capital to Bukhara. 'Ismail moved the capital of the Samanid dynasty from Samarkand to Bukhara' after Nasr I's death in August 892; infobox 'Samarkand (819-892); Bukhara (892-999)'.

893: Isma'il takes Taraz from the Karluks. 'In 893, Ismail took the city of Taraz', 'the capital of the Karluk Turks'; the Samanid page: 'Ismail Samani invaded the territories of the Karluk Turks, taking Talas'.

Spring 900: Isma'il and Amr ibn al-Layth meet at Balkh. 'The two sides fought in Balkh, northern Afghanistan during the spring of 900'; the caliph al-Mu'tadid had 'sent Ismail a letter urging him to fight Amr-i Laith'.

900: Khorasan is Isma'il's. Amr 'was captured, and some of his troops switched sides'; the caliph 'invested Ismail with Khorasan'; the Samanid page: 'Ismail was thereafter recognized as the ruler of all of Khorasan and Transoxiana by the caliph'. The Samanid page gives the battle as spring 900 in one place and 901 in another.
900: the Balkh campaign ends with Amr in captivity (sent to Baghdad and executed in April 902, Amr page).
900: Isma'il invades Tabaristan. 'Ismail decided to take advantage of the caliph's grant by sending an army to Tabaristan'; 'The Samanids now demanded the cession of Gurgan'.

3 October 900: Muhammad ibn Zayd dies and the Samanids take Tabaristan. 'the Samanids prevailed, and the severely wounded Muhammad was captured'; 'He died on the next day, 3 October 900'; 'the Samanids took over the province'.
October 900: the fighting for Tabaristan and Gurgan ends.

901: the Samanid army takes Ray. The page has an army sent 'into northern Persia in 901' that 'managed to conquer several other cities including Ray'; the caliph invested Isma'il 'with Khorasan, Tabaristan, Ray, and Isfahan' (Isfahan is a grant and is not drawn). Ray had been handed to the Saffarids in 897 (Amr page).
By 911: Sistan under Samanid control. 'by 911, Sistan was under complete Samanid control' (the Saffarid page: the Samanids 'finally expelled the Saffarids from Sistan' in 912).
December 913: the Zaydi Hasan al-Utrush defeats the Samanid army. 'Hasan managed to inflict a crushing defeat upon it in December 913 at Burdidah on the river Burrud west of Chalus.'
914: the Samanids, whose amir Ahmad was murdered in January 914, give up the fight for Tabaristan.

January 914: Tabaristan and Gurgan are lost to the Zaydis. 'Reign: January 914 - January/February 917'; al-Utrush 'was soon able to extend his control over all the old Zaydid domains, including both Tabaristan and Gurgan'.

After 917: the Sajid Yusuf takes Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray. 'After Ibn al-Furat regained the vizierate in 917, Yusuf conquered Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray from the Samanids.' The Zaydi pages also have al-Utrush taking Ray (undated); the pages disagree on who held it.

c. 919: Ray reverts to a governor of the Samanids after Yusuf's defeat (bridging). The Yusuf page: 'In 919 the Sajid was defeated' and he was 'imprisoned for three years'; it does not say who held Ray, but in 924 Yusuf took it 'from its governor, who had rebelled against the Samanids', so a governor answering to the Samanids held it in between. Which page wins for Ray 914-928: the Yusuf page, the only one that dates Ray (917, 919, 924, 925), keeps it with the Samanids until 917; the Nasr II page's 'Ray and Tabaristan were taken by the Zaydi Alid Hasan al-Utrush' is undated, and the Zaydi dossier's Ray gain of 914 (confidence 1) is not carried here.

922: Sistan returns to a Saffarid emir. 'Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad restored independence', table 922-963; the Nasr II page says 'The Abbasids managed to recover Sistan for the last time' without a year.

922: the restored Saffarid emirate is a vassal of Bukhara. The Saffarid page: 'their role was reduced to that of vassals of the Samanids and their successors' (undated), and its table lists 'Samanid occupation 913-922 CE' before Abu Ja'far Ahmad's '922-963 CE'; the Samanid page already has the Saffarids 'a minor tributary in Sistan' after 901, and the Khalaf page that Khalaf 'had neglected to send the customary tribute to the Samanid amir' (979). The tie from 922 is the reading that joins these (the year of the tie is bridged).

924: Ray falls to Yusuf again. In 924 he 'conquered Ray from its governor, who had rebelled against the Samanids' (the governor is not named), so the Samanid hold was already lost in fact; after he left for Hamadan 'the people of Ray expelled his officials' and 'In 925 the Sajid briefly returned to Ray'. The page does not say who held Ray from 925 to the Samanid general Asfar's conquest of 928.

928: the Samanid general Asfar takes Tabaristan and Ray. 'In 928, Asfar ibn Shiruya, a Dailamite military leader who now served the Samanids, conquered Tabaristan and Ray'; 'Ray and Tabaristan were taken by the Zaydi Alid Hasan al-Utrush' earlier (undated).

930: Makan ibn Kaki seizes Tabaristan and Gurgan. Makan 'used this opportunity to seize Tabaristan and Gurgan from the Samanids'. The Makan page: 'in 930, Makan managed to recover Tabaristan, extend his control over most of Gurgan'.

c. 930: Ray passes to Asfar ibn Shiruya, who had taken it for the Samanids in 928 (bridging). The Asfar page: he acted first 'apparently as a delegate of the Samanids, but thereafter as a sovereign ruler'; 'Asfar now expanded his domains over Ray, Qazvin and other parts of Jibal' and he ruled 'Tabaristan and northern Jibal briefly from 928 to 930'; 'he was overwhelmed and killed by Mardavij, most likely in 931'. The page gives no year for his break with the Samanids. Ray then passes to Mardavij in 931 (Ziyarid dossier /ledger/2) and is held for tribute from 933.

931: Makan withdraws under Samanid pressure. He 'was forced to abandon these regions a year later, due to the threat that Samanids posed' (Nasr II page); the Makan page: 'which he was forced to abandon in 931, bowing to pressure by the Samanid ruler Nasr II' (it applies this to Nishapur). Both pages then have him return to Tabaristan, where Mardavij defeated him, so the Samanid hold on Tabaristan and Gurgan in 931-932 was nominal; confidence lowered to 2.

c. 932: the Ziyarid Mardavij conquers Tabaristan and, with it, Gurgan. Makan 'then returned to Tabaristan, where he was defeated by the Ziyarid ruler Mardavij, who managed to conquer the region' (Nasr II page, no year; the Makan page: 'Mardavij launched an attack that conquered Tabaristan', undated, after Makan won a first engagement in 931); 932 is the Ziyarid dossier's year and is bridged here. Gurgan goes with it by inference: Mardavij had to 'surrender Gurgan' to Nasr in 933, so he held it. The chain is Samanids (931, Makan out) to Makan back in Tabaristan to Mardavij; the Samanid claim passes to the Ziyarids, while the Ziyarid dossier books the same moves as gains from the Zaydi state (ended 928) and from Makan.

c. 932: the Banu Ilyas settle in Kerman as nominal Samanid vassals (bridging). The Banu Ilyas page: after the failed 929 coup against Nasr, Abu 'Ali Muhammad b. Ilyas 'fled south, eventually arriving at Kerman in 932'; he 'acknowledged either the Samanids or the Buyids as his overlords but was effectively independent'; the Nasr II page has Nasr appoint Makan governor of Kerman; the Mansur page calls the Banu Ilyas 'nominal Samanid vassals' (undated). 'Samanid and later Buyid attempts to expel him from Kerman' failed.
933: Mardavij cedes Gurgan and pays tribute. Mardavij made peace 'to surrender Gurgan and pay tribute to Nasr for his possession of Ray'.

933: the Ziyarids hold Ray for tribute. Mardavij agreed 'to pay tribute to Nasr for his possession of Ray'; after his murder in 935 Vushmgir accepted 'Samanid overlordship' and ceded Gurgan to Makan (Nasr II page, undated). The Samanid page has Nasr II make Vushmgir 'his vassal' in 935: the same relation under a new ruler, so no second vassal_start.

935: Vushmgir conquers Gurgan from the Samanid side. After Mardavij's murder in 935 Makan 'immediately left Kirman, secured his appointment as governor of Gurgan from Nasr', and 'Vushmgir managed to repel the attack and even conquer Gurgan' (Nasr II page; the Ziyarid dossier, from the Ziyarid page: he 'wrested Gorgan from Samanid control', undated). The year is the 935 of the page's context; the order inside 935 is bridged, the loss coming before Nasr II's re-establishment of control.

935: Nasr II re-establishes Samanid control in Gurgan and makes Vushmgir a vassal. 'In 935, Nasr II re-established Samanid control in Gurgan and made Mardavij's successor Vushmgir his vassal'; the Nasr II page has Vushmgir 'recognizing Samanid overlordship and ceding Gurgan to Makan', Nasr's appointed governor. The Ziyarid dossier dates the hand-over to Makan 936 (its /ledger/12) and names Makan as counterpart; this ledger keeps the Samanid page's 935.

962: Alp Tigin conquers Ghazna from the Lawiks as a nominal Samanid vassal. 'Alp Tigin, nominal vassal of the Samanids, conquered Ghazna in 962 from the Lawik dynasty'; the same page: 'In 962, one of the ghulams, Alp Tigin, commander of the army in Khorasan, seized Ghazna and established himself there' and 'His successors, however, including Sabuktigin, continued to rule as Samanid "governors"'. Ghazna was never Samanid land: the Lawik page has Alp-Tegin 'wrested the town from its ruler Abu Bakr Lawik' (the Lawiks 'after 877, ruled under the Hindu Shahi suzerainty'). So this is a vassal_start, not a loss (the earlier 962 loss was withdrawn after the review); the year of the tie is the page's 962, its reading as vassalage is mine (confidence 2). The Ghaznavid dossier has no matching vassal_start; it founds in 962 from the Lawiks.

968: Adud al-Dawla conquers Kerman from the Banu Ilyas. The Banu Ilyas page's infobox gives 'Buyid conquest: 968'; the Mansur page: 'Adud al-Dawla wrested Kerman from the Banu Ilyas, nominal Samanid vassals'. The Cliopatria 970 shape drops Kerman (about 124 thousand km2 of its 320 thousand km2 loss) two years later; the Buyid dossier dates Adud's conquest of Kerman 967.

980: the Karakhanids seize Isfijab. The Nuh II page: 'In 980 they struck again, seizing Isfijab' (after the capture of the upper Zarafshan Valley, undated). The location is read from the name (Isfijab = Sayram, by Shymkent). The Kara-Khanid page lists Isfijab among the conquests of 'Between 990 and 992', a conflict between the two pages; the Kara-Khanid dossier has no 980 gain. Cliopatria's Samanid shape keeps the Shymkent area to 999.

981: the Ziyarid vassals lose their last land. The Qabus page: 'Adud then invaded and conquered Tabaristan; in 981 Adud's brother Mu'ayyad al-Dawla took Gurgan', and 'Qabus and Fakhr al-Dawla were forced to flee to Samanid Khurasan'; 'The Samanids sent a force to take back the provinces, but were unsuccessful' (undated). The Mansur page: the Buyids expelled 'the Samanids' Ziyarid vassals from Tabaristan and Gurgan' (undated); the Ziyarid dossier has the Buyid takeover of Tabaristan in 980 and of Gorgan in 981. This replaces the earlier c. 979 (bridged from the end of Cliopatria's Ziyarid row); Ray is dropped from the region because the Ziyarids had lost it to the Buyids in 943 (Ziyarid dossier /ledger/15).

region.text: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara

ledger.note: 990: the Kara-Khanid Hasan Bughra Khan attacks the Samanids. 'Between 990 and 992, Hasan took Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand, and the Samanid capital Bukhara' (Kara-Khanid page; the Kara-Khanid dossier opens its contest in 990 too). The Nuh II page has the Karakhanids earlier on the Zarafshan and at Isfijab (980) and dates the 'full-scale invasion at the end of 991', so the 990 start is not corroborated by it (a range on the page, confidence 2). Bukhara itself is the 992 occupation below.

992: Harun Bughra Khan occupies Bukhara. In 992 he 'captured Bukhara, the Samanid capital' (Samanid page; the Ghaznavids page: 'They occupied Bukhara in 992, establishing in Transoxania the Kara-Khanid Khanate'; the Nuh II page: 'the Karakhanids entered the capital in the late spring of 992').
992: the Kara-Khanids leave Bukhara. 'Hasan Bughra Khan died in 992 due to an illness, and the Samanids returned to Bukhara' (Kara-Khanid page). The final occupation is 999 (the loss below).

998: Mahmud is confirmed in Balkh, Tirmidh and Herat. 'That year, in 998, Mahmud then travelled to Balkh and paid homage to Amir Abu'l-Harith Mansur b. Nur II' and 'After accession to the throne, the Samanid Amir Mansur II confirmed Mahmud the possession of Ghazni, Bust, eastern Khurasanian towns of Balkh, Tirmidh, and Herat' (Mahmud page; the Ghaznavid dossier books it as a gain, confidence 2); the page's 999 entry also has 'Gained Balkh, Herat, Tirmidh, Bust from the Samanids'. A confirmation under Samanid suzerainty, so the land leaves Samanid government for a vassal governor: the loss is booked here, inside the Ghaznavid vassalage of 962-999. Earlier in the decade (Mahmud page): on 23 October 994 Mahmud 'joined his father Sabuktigin in the capture of Khorasan from the rebel Fa'iq' and took 'the command of the troops of Khurasan in place of Abu 'Ali Simjuri'; in 995 Abu 'Ali and Fa'iq 'expelled Mahmud from Nishapur' (Nuh II page) and in 996 Mahmud 'retook it without a fight'. The Samanid page is silent on 994-998; the Simjurids page has no dated running text.

999: the Ilig occupies Bukhara for good. 'the shrunken Samanid amirate came to an inglorious end when the Ilig occupied Bukhara definitively in 999'; the Karakhanids received Transoxiana and 'the Oxus River thus became the boundary'.
999: the contest for Bukhara ends with the Kara-Khanid occupation.

minus.text: Khorasan
Balkh, Herat and Tirmidh

region.text: the rest of Khorasan up to the Oxus (Balkh, Herat and Tirmidh went in 998)

ledger.note: 999: Khorasan goes to the Ghaznavids. 'The Samanid domains were split up between the Ghaznavids, who gained Khorasan' and the Karakhanids; the Ghaznavids page has Mahmud receiving 'the governorship of Khurasan' on his accession in 998. Balkh, Herat and Tirmidh are left out of the region because the 998 loss above already carries them.

999: the Saffarid tribute to Bukhara ends with the state. The Saffarid page has the later Saffarids 'reduced to that of vassals of the Samanids and their successors' and Mahmud of Ghazni invading Sistan in 1002, three years later, when he 'dethroned Khalaf ibn Ahmad and finally ended the Saffarid dynasty'.

999: the Ghaznavid tie to Bukhara ends. 'The Oxus River was decided as the borders between the two empires' (Mahmud page, 999), after 'A brief peace agreement was concluded ensuring Mahmud's control of Herat and Balkh'.

region.text: Samarkand, Farghana and Tashkent, the governorships of Nuh, Ahmad and Yahya ibn Asad

ledger.note: 999: the formal allegiance to the caliph ends with the state. The Abbasid dossier ends the tie in 999 (its /ledger/73-74) on the page's 'Karakhanids took Bukhara from the Samanids'; the page gives the dynasty 'from 819 to 999' and no later caliphal tie.
999: the Samanid amirate ends. The dynasty ruled 'from 819 to 999'; Isma'il Muntasir was killed in 1005 and 'His death marked the defeat of the last attempt to restore the Samanid state'.

wars.name: Samanid Civil War of 888
wars.outcome: Nasr I and his brother Isma'il fought over the distribution of tax money; Isma'il was victorious and took control of the state.
wars.note: A war within the dynasty; it moved no external border.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Taraz
wars.outcome: Isma'il took Taraz, capital of the Karluk Turks; further campaigns in 903 'secured the Samanid boundaries'.

wars.name: Samanid–Saffarid war
wars.outcome: Samanid victory at Balkh in spring 900; Amr captured; Isma'il invested with Khorasan.
wars.note: The Samanid page also gives 901 for the battle.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Muhammad ibn Zayd defeated and dead on 3 October 900; the Samanids took Tabaristan, Gurgan and, in 901, Ray.

wars.name: Samanid takeover of Saffarid Sistan
wars.outcome: Sistan under complete Samanid control by 911.

wars.name: Zaydi restoration in Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Samanid army defeated at Burdidah in December 913; Tabaristan and Gurgan lost in January 914.

wars.name: Sajid conquest of Ray
wars.outcome: Yusuf took Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray after 917, was defeated and imprisoned in 919, and took Ray again in 924 from a governor who had rebelled against the Samanids; he held it briefly (925).

wars.name: Samanid reconquest of Tabaristan and Makan's revolt
wars.outcome: Asfar took Tabaristan and Ray in 928 and ruled them as a sovereign until his death in about 931; Makan seized Tabaristan and Gurgan in 930 and left a year later; Mardavij then took Tabaristan.

wars.name: Samanid–Ziyarid war
wars.outcome: Mardavij conquered Tabaristan (about 932), ceded Gurgan and paid tribute for Ray in 933; after his murder in 935 Vushmgir took Gurgan and Nasr II re-established Samanid control there and made him a vassal (935).

wars.name: Alp-Tigin's conquest of Ghazna
wars.outcome: After the succession crisis of 961 Alp-Tigin, a Samanid slave commander and nominal vassal, fled to Ghazna and in 962 wrested it from Abu Bakr Lawik after a siege of four months; the Lawiks recaptured it around 965 and were uprooted by 977. The Samanids were not a belligerent.
wars.note: The Mansur page (961 succession crisis) and the Samanid page ('conquered Ghazna in 962 from the Lawik dynasty') agree on the year.

wars.name: Samanid-backed campaign against Khalaf of Sistan
wars.outcome: Khalaf was defeated in August 979 by a Samanid-backed army; no territorial change.
wars.note: Khalaf had neglected the customary tribute to Bukhara.

wars.name: Kara-Khanid and Ghaznavid conquest of the Samanid domains
wars.outcome: Isfijab, Ferghana, Ilaq, Samarkand and Bukhara attacked from 990; Bukhara occupied in 992 and abandoned on Hasan's death; Bukhara taken definitively in 999 and the domains split between the Ghaznavids (Khorasan) and the Karakhanids (Transoxiana) along the Oxus.
wars.note: 990 is the Kara-Khanid page's start of 'Between 990 and 992'; the Samanid page dates Bukhara to 992 and 999.

wars.name: Samanid civil war of 994-996 (Fa'iq and the Simjurids)
wars.outcome: Sabuktigin and Mahmud captured Khorasan from the rebel Fa'iq on 23 October 994 and won at Tus on 22 July 995 after Abu 'Ali and Fa'iq had beaten Mahmud at Nishapur in April 995; Mahmud retook Nishapur in 996 and reconsolidated power in Khurasan.
wars.note: No border change is dated; the Samanid page is silent and the Simjurids page has no dated running text.

certainty.note: Governorships and steppe frontiers (Karluks, Oghuz, Kimek) are approximate; Sistan, Tabaristan, Gurgan and Ray changed status repeatedly and are drawn soft.
The 999 partition made the Oxus 'the boundary between the two rival empires'.

notes:
Cliopatria's Samanid row is 886..999 in twelve shapes; the dossier adds 819-885 (the governorships), 914-921 and 998-999, and replaces the shapes' overreach: 900-910 is the 900 shape minus Fars, Kerman and Sistan (Saffarid remnant), 914-921 is minus the Zaydi land, 922-961 is minus Fars, Tabaristan, Sistan and Ghazna with its hinterland, 962-999 is minus Sistan (carried as a vassal from 922), and 998-999 also loses Balkh, Herat and Tirmidh. The Cliopatria 898-899 shape is replaced by the 896 shape. The infobox area (928 est. 2.85 M km2) is 7 percent below Cliopatria's 3.06 M km2.
Repair pass (after the adversarial review): (1) Ghazna was Lawik land, taken in 962 by Alp Tigin, a 'nominal vassal of the Samanids'; the 962 loss is now a vassal_start (962-999) and Ghazna with its hinterland (the Cliopatria Ghaznavid 962 shape, which lies wholly inside the Samanid 922 shape) is out of the 922-961 shapes; the 980 drop is likewise the Cliopatria Ghaznavid 980 shape. (2) Gurgan: lost with Tabaristan in 932, ceded back in 933, lost to Vushmgir and recovered in 935 (Nasr II page; the Ziyarid dossier has the hand-over to Makan in 936). (3) Ray: the Yusuf page wins for 914-928 because it is the only page that dates Ray (917 Sajid, 919 defeat, 924 conquest from a rebel governor, 925 brief return); the Nasr II page's Zaydi capture of Ray is undated, so the Zaydi dossier's Ray gain of 914 (confidence 1) and the Sajid dossier's missing 919 loss are not matched here and need the other authors' attention; a c. 930 loss to Asfar ibn Shiruya follows the Asfar and Mardavij pages. (4) Mirror vassal events added for the Abbasids (819-999), the Tahirids (821-873), the Ghaznavids (962-999) and the Banu Ilyas of Kerman (932-968). (5) 998 loss of Balkh, Herat and Tirmidh to the Ghaznavids (a confirmation by Mansur II, Mahmud page); the 999 loss of Khorasan leaves them out. (6) The Kara-Khanid contest now opens in 990 (Kara-Khanid page) with the 992 occupation of Bukhara as its own pair; the Nuh II page has the Karakhanids at Isfijab in 980 and a full invasion at the end of 991, which conflicts with the Kara-Khanid page's 990-992 and is for ia-01 to settle. (7) Ziyarid vassalage now ends in 981 (Qabus page) instead of c. 979.
Still unsettled: the 960 drop (east edge 76.6E to 75.2E: the Abd al-Malik I page has no territory), the 197 thousand km2 of the 970 drop that is not Kerman, the individual conquests behind the 980 shape, the Isfijab location (read from the name), who held Ray 925-928 and Kerman before the Banu Ilyas, and Herat as an Asad governorship in 819 although the Saffarid page calls it Tahirid in 870 (the Abbasid dossier draws Herat as a Samanid vassal from 819 to 999 and needs review). Not on any page opened as vassals: Chaghaniyan (Muhtajids), Khuttal, Ushrusana, the Ma'munids of Khwarazm (the Nuh II page has the Khwarazm governor 'only nominally' accepting Nuh's authority and a Khwarazm Shah holding the south 'as a Samanid vassal', undated). Counterparts needing dossiers: Makan ibn Kaki (930-940), Asfar ibn Shiruya (928-931), Banu Ilyas of Kerman (932-968), Lawik dynasty (c. 750-977). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Isfijab (a place, used as Shymkent 100 km); Ushrusana, Chaghaniyan, Khuttal, Jibal (unused). Page budget 5, exceeded in the repair pass: the review findings required ten more pages (Kara-Khanid Khanate, Mahmud of Ghazni, Lawik dynasty, Asfar ibn Shiruya, Makan ibn Kaki, Banu Ilyas, Nuh II, Qabus, Simjurids, Abd al-Malik I).
